chapter: Bob Lyons band and New Orleans musicians
title: Big Cornish, a fight and old friends
summary: Talk about Big Corny, a drunken birthday quarrel, Guy Kelly's funeral, Andy Anderson and a band with Kid Allen and Alex Scott before Mexico.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Ask him if he knew Big Cornish.
Did you know Corny? Who? Big Corny? He's a big little Big Corny. He was another chicken one too. He was about six feet tall too. He was tall. And then she called me and him, Buck and Jeff.
Tell him I heard he had a fight with Corny.

Say, he heard you had a fight with Corny. I think I heard about that. I think it was on my birthday that night, I got drunk, you know. And Tony told me to stop playing, you know. Stop drinking. I said, oh, you ain't got nothing to do with me. I said, the white people, they was giving it to me, helping me to celebrate. And Tony got mad. I said, you big son got busted. I said, go ahead, sit on, sit on, sit on. And then after he told me to come over, you know. Zip would play with his dad, you know. You know Zip, don't you? Kid Vidi, you know them? Yeah. He always would play with me. And let me say, what's the name? Guy Kelly. Guy Kelly. He died in Chicago or New York? Yeah, I played taps for him. Huh? I played taps at his funeral. Oh yeah? In Chicago, huh? Yeah. In Chicago, huh? Yeah. Yeah. In Chicago. Yeah. Yeah. In Chicago. Yeah. He died in Chicago or New York? Yeah, I played taps for him. Huh? I played taps at his funeral. Oh yeah? In Chicago, huh? Yeah. Now Lee, is he living here? Yeah. Yeah, Lee was down there, but he was sick. He's sick now? Yeah, he was something like me. He was constipated. He used to suffer, but I just started to start to be constipated about a week, nine, almost a week. That made me sick so bad, you see. He used to be a sick man before he left here, you know. We used to always try to help him out, you know. And I heard, buddy, I heard that, uh, Lewis Armstrong kept him out there. Yeah, yeah.
Tell him I heard that when Cornish swung at him, he'd run between his legs.
Say, heard that when Cornish swung at you, you'd run between his legs. Yeah.
I did tell you, I thought that. No, Andy Anderson. Andy Anderson. The trumpet player. The trumpet player.
He said, Andy Anderson, the trumpet player is a young fella.
Oh, oh. He told me about it.
He told him about it. Yeah. You know, Anderson? Yeah.

Yeah. I used to play with him too. Emily's cousin, Earl Foster. You never heard of him, eh? Yeah, I know him. That's Anderson's cousin. Yeah. That's a funny story to hear. Tell it, you know. Yeah, after he came up there that night to get me, you know.
Yeah, but he wasn't doing nothing.
He used to come meet me on his job, you know. We'd come home together, you know. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

Mm-hm. Kid Allen and Albert Martin, he's there too. You remember that Albedroom? Yeah. And Alex Scott. We had a band there, bass player. We had a band there. That's where, you know, left and went to Mexico, you know. And after that, when we come back, when I got a bass player, he left too. He used to wouldn't go nowhere but right up the country. He's kind of his daddy. Yeah, I remember. Tell me his son is almost as good as him now. Who, Red Allen? Huh? Who, Red Allen? Yeah. You don't know his son, eh? No, I don't know him. That's what they tell me. You know Red Allen? I don't know his son. No, I don't know his son either.
